ai.description: This file defines the core logic for the consensus process in the Ripple (XRPL) ledger system. It provides a highly generic, template-based Consensus class that manages the state and progression of consensus rounds among network peers. The class is parameterized by an Adaptor, allowing it to be used with different ledger and transaction set types. The consensus process involves collecting proposals from peers, tracking their positions, managing disputes over transactions, and determining when consensus has been reached or failed. The class handles transitions between different consensus phases (open, establish, accepted), manages timing and round progression, and provides mechanisms for pausing, simulating, and forcibly accepting consensus. It also includes logic for handling peers that fall out of sync, managing close times, and updating the local node's position based on peer input. The file includes utility functions for determining when to close a ledger, checking for consensus, and serializing the consensus state to JSON for monitoring or debugging. The MonitoredMode inner class tracks and manages the current consensus mode (proposing, observing, wrong ledger, etc.), ensuring the Adaptor is notified of mode changes. Overall, this file encapsulates the state machine and algorithms required for distributed agreement on ledger state in the XRPL network.

This file implements the core logic for the RCLConsensus class, which manages the consensus process in the Ripple (XRPL) ledger system. It defines the RCLConsensus and its nested Adaptor class, which acts as an interface between the consensus engine and the rest of the application. The Adaptor handles acquiring ledgers and transaction sets, sharing proposals and transactions with peers, proposing new ledgers, managing open transactions, and tracking consensus state. It also manages the process of closing and accepting ledgers, including building new ledgers, applying transactions, handling disputes, and validating ledgers. The file includes mechanisms for voting on fees and amendments, handling negative UNL (Unique Node List) votes, and detecting potential censorship of transactions. It provides detailed logging and status notifications to peers, and manages validator keys and operating modes. The RclConsensusLogger class is used for detailed timing and logging of consensus events. Overall, this file is central to the operation of distributed consensus in the XRPL node software, coordinating ledger agreement, transaction application, and network communication during consensus rounds.

This file implements core consensus logic for the XRPL (Ripple) ledger. It provides three main functions: shouldCloseLedger, which determines if the current ledger should be closed based on transaction activity, proposer participation, timing, and consensus parameters; checkConsensusReached, which checks if a sufficient percentage of nodes have agreed on a proposal to declare consensus, considering edge cases like stalling or timeouts; and checkConsensus, which orchestrates the consensus process by evaluating proposer counts, agreement levels, timing, and consensus thresholds to return the current consensus state (No, Yes, MovedOn, or Expired). The code includes detailed logging and handles various edge cases to ensure robust consensus decision-making in a distributed ledger environment.

This file defines the DisputedTx template class, which manages the state and voting process for transactions that are disputed during the XRPL consensus process. Each DisputedTx instance tracks a specific transaction, the local node's vote, and the votes of peer nodes. It provides methods to set and update votes, determine if consensus has stalled, and serialize its state to JSON. The class uses counters for 'yes' and 'no' votes, tracks voting rounds, and applies consensus parameters to decide when to change votes or consider a transaction stalled. Logging is integrated for debugging and informational purposes.

Once the ledger is closed, servers avalanche to consensus on the candidate transaction set and the close time. When consensus is reached, servers build a new last closed ledger by starting with the previous last closed ledger and applying the consensus transaction set. In the normal case, servers will all agree on both the last closed ledger and the consensus transaction set. The goal is to give the network the highest chances of arriving at the same conclusion on all servers.

At all times during the consensus process the open ledger remains open with the same transaction set, and has new transactions applied. It will likely have transactions that are also in the new last closed ledger. Valid transactions received during the consensus process will only be in the open ledger.

This directory holds the types and classes needed to connect the generic consensus algorithm to the rippled-specific instance of consensus.

`RCLCxTx` adapts a `SHAMapItem` transaction.

`RCLCxTxSet` adapts a `SHAMap` to represent a set of transactions.

`RCLCxLedger` adapts a `Ledger`.

`RCLConsensus` is implements the requirements of the generic

`Consensus` class by connecting to the rest of the `rippled`

application.

ai.description: This file defines the ConsensusParms struct, which encapsulates various configuration parameters for the consensus process in the Ripple (XRPL) system. These parameters include timeouts and intervals for validation and proposal freshness, minimum consensus percentages, ledger timing constraints, and settings for the Avalanche consensus state machine. The AvalancheState enum and AvalancheCutoff struct are used to manage state transitions during consensus, with a map defining cutoff thresholds for each state. The file also provides the getNeededWeight function, which determines the required consensus percentage and potential next state based on the current state, elapsed time, and round counts. Overall, the file centralizes consensus-related constants and logic to facilitate robust and tunable consensus operations.

This header file defines the CanonicalTXSet class, which manages a set of transactions in a canonical (deterministic) order for the XRPL (XRP Ledger) system. The class uses a nested Key class to uniquely identify and order transactions based on account, sequence, and transaction ID. CanonicalTXSet provides methods to insert, remove, and iterate over transactions, as well as to reset the set with a new salt value. The set is implemented as a map from Key to transaction pointers, ensuring consistent ordering and efficient access. The class is designed to facilitate transaction processing and ordering in the ledger application.

This file implements the core logic for the 'tx' RPC handler in the XRPL (Ripple) server. The main classes are TxQ (the queue itself), TxQ::FeeMetrics (for fee escalation and queue sizing), TxQ::MaybeTx (a queued transaction), and TxQ::TxQAccount (per-account transaction management).

This file defines the core logic for the consensus process in the Ripple (XRPL) ledger system. It provides a highly generic, template-based Consensus class that manages the state and progression of consensus rounds among network peers. The class is parameterized by an Adaptor, allowing it to be used with different ledger and transaction set types. The consensus process involves collecting proposals from peers, tracking their positions, managing disputes over transactions, and determining when consensus has been reached or failed. The class handles transitions between different consensus phases (open, establish, accepted), manages timing and round progression, and provides mechanisms for pausing, simulating, and forcibly accepting consensus. It also includes logic for handling peers that fall out of sync, managing close times, and updating the local node's position based on peer input. The file includes utility functions for determining when to close a ledger, checking for consensus, and serializing the consensus state to JSON for monitoring or debugging. The MonitoredMode inner class tracks and manages the current consensus mode (proposing, observing, wrong ledger, etc.), ensuring the Adaptor is notified of mode changes. Overall, this file encapsulates the state machine and algorithms required for distributed agreement on ledger state in the XRPL network.

This file implements methods for the STValidation class in the Ripple (XRPL) protocol. It provides functionality for copying and moving validation objects, defines the format of a validation object (including required and optional fields), and implements methods to retrieve various fields such as signing hash, ledger hash, consensus hash, signing time, and seen time. It also includes methods to check if a validation is valid (by verifying the signature), if it is a full validation, and to retrieve the signature and serialized form of the validation. The code ensures that validations are properly formatted and cryptographically verified according to the protocol's requirements.

This file implements a set of invariant checks for the XRPL (XRP Ledger) transaction processing engine. Each class represents a specific invariant that must be maintained during ledger state transitions caused by transactions. The invariants ensure the integrity, consistency, and security of the ledger by validating that certain conditions hold before and after transactions are applied. Key invariants include: ensuring transaction fees are non-negative and within limits (TransactionFeeCheck), preventing the creation of XRP out of thin air (XRPNotCreated), checking for valid account balances (XRPBalanceChecks), disallowing invalid offers (NoBadOffers), ensuring escrow amounts are valid (NoZeroEscrow), preventing unauthorized account deletions (AccountRootsNotDeleted, AccountRootsDeletedClean), ensuring ledger entry types are consistent (LedgerEntryTypesMatch), disallowing XRP trust lines (NoXRPTrustLines), enforcing correct freeze semantics on trust lines (NoDeepFreezeTrustLinesWithoutFreeze, TransfersNotFrozen), validating new account creation (ValidNewAccountRoot), checking NFT page structure and NFT mint/burn counts (ValidNFTokenPage, NFTokenCountTracking), validating clawback operations (ValidClawback), ensuring correct issuance and management of multi-party tokens (ValidMPTIssuance), enforcing permissioned domain and DEX rules (ValidPermissionedDomain, ValidPermissionedDEX), and maintaining Automated Market Maker (AMM) pool invariants (ValidAMM). Each class provides visitEntry methods to observe ledger changes and finalize methods to enforce the invariant after transaction application, logging fatal errors and rejecting transactions if invariants are violated.

ai.description: This file implements the doAccountInfo function, which handles the 'account_info' RPC request in the XRPL (Ripple) server. The function processes input parameters to identify an account, validates and parses the account identifier, and looks up the specified ledger. If the account exists, it retrieves and returns detailed account data, including account flags, optional signer lists, and (if requested) queued transactions for the account. The function supports various feature flags and API versions, and provides error handling for missing or malformed input, non-existent accounts, and invalid parameters. The response is constructed as a JSON object containing the requested account information or error details.

content: For consensus to be considered healthy, the peers on the network should largely remain in sync with one another. It is particularly important for the validators to remain in sync, because that is required for participation in consensus. However, the network tolerates some validators being out of sync.  Fundamentally, network health is a function of validators reaching consensus on sets of recently submitted transactions.

This file implements the TransactionAcquire class, which manages the process of acquiring a transaction set (SHAMap) from peers in a distributed ledger network (such as XRPL). The class handles timeouts, peer selection, and the step-by-step acquisition of SHAMap nodes, including root and non-root nodes. It tracks progress, handles failures, and triggers further requests as needed. When the transaction set is fully acquired or acquisition fails, it notifies the application via a job queue. The class ensures robustness by retrying with additional peers, handling invalid data, and managing state transitions between incomplete, complete, and failed acquisition states.

This file implements the core network operations logic for the XRPL server (rippled). The main class, NetworkOPsImp, manages the server's operating mode, transaction processing (both synchronous and asynchronous), consensus participation, ledger publication, and subscription management for various real-time data streams (such as ledgers, transactions, validations, and account history). It handles state transitions (disconnected, connected, syncing, tracking, full), processes incoming and outgoing transactions, manages transaction batches, and coordinates consensus rounds. The class also provides mechanisms for clients to subscribe/unsubscribe to server events and account-specific updates, including historical transaction streaming. It tracks server fee metrics, publishes server and consensus status, and manages resource usage. The implementation includes detailed state accounting for monitoring and reporting, and supports both standalone and networked operation modes. The file also contains logic for handling book offers, peer status, and validator list management, ensuring the server stays in sync with the network and provides up-to-date information to clients.

This header file defines a set of classes for handling cross-chain (XChain) bridge transactions in the Ripple (XRPL) codebase. Each class represents a specific type of cross-chain transaction, such as creating or modifying a bridge, making claims, committing transactions, creating claim IDs, and adding attestations. All these classes inherit from a base Transactor class and implement standard transaction lifecycle methods: preflight, preclaim, and doApply. The file also defines a maximum number of account create claims and uses type aliases for some classes. The design supports extensible and modular handling of cross-chain operations within the XRPL transaction processing framework.

This file defines core data structures and logic for managing and tracking validations in the XRPL consensus process. It introduces configuration parameters (ValidationParms) for validation timing and freshness, a SeqEnforcer utility to enforce sequence number rules, and the main Validations template class. The Validations class manages current and historical validations, enforces validation sequence rules, tracks trusted/untrusted validators, and maintains a ledger trie for efficient consensus operations. It provides methods for adding, expiring, and querying validations, updating trust status, and determining preferred ledgers for consensus. The code is thread-safe, using mutexes to protect shared state, and is designed to be adaptable via an Adaptor template parameter for integration with different ledger and validation types.

This file defines the ApplyViewBase class, an abstract base class in the Ripple ledger implementation. ApplyViewBase inherits from ApplyView and RawView, and provides a set of virtual methods for interacting with and modifying the ledger state, such as reading, inserting, updating, and erasing ledger entries, as well as handling transactions and fees. The class manages state changes using an ApplyStateTable and maintains references to a base ReadView and apply flags. Constructors and assignment operators are mostly deleted to prevent copying, ensuring controlled usage. The class is intended for internal use in the ledger application process, providing a foundation for derived classes to implement specific ledger modification logic.

This file implements the core logic for the transaction queue (TxQ) in the XRPL server. The TxQ manages transactions that cannot be immediately applied to the open ledger, handling queuing, prioritization, and eventual application or removal. Key features include: calculation of fee levels paid and required, dynamic adjustment of queue and fee escalation parameters based on ledger activity, logic for replacing or removing transactions in the queue, and mechanisms for applying queued transactions when conditions allow. The queue enforces per-account and global limits, supports transaction replacement with higher fees, and penalizes accounts for repeated failures. The file also provides metrics and RPC reporting for queue status and fee levels. Configuration is supported via a setup function that reads parameters from the server config. The main classes are TxQ (the queue itself), TxQ::FeeMetrics (for fee escalation and queue sizing), TxQ::MaybeTx (a queued transaction), and TxQ::TxQAccount (per-account transaction management).

This file implements the LedgerMaster class, which is a core component of the XRPL server responsible for managing the lifecycle, state, and history of ledgers. It handles tracking the current, validated, and published ledgers, manages ledger acquisition and validation, and coordinates the publication and storage of ledgers. The class ensures ledger continuity, handles missing or out-of-sync ledgers, and manages fetch packs for ledger synchronization between peers. It also processes held transactions, manages pathfinding requests, and interacts with other subsystems such as the order book database, fee tracking, and amendment management. The file includes logic for advancing the ledger state, handling consensus results, and maintaining caches and history for efficient ledger retrieval. It is central to the operation of the XRPL node, ensuring ledger integrity, synchronization, and network participation.

This file implements the core logic for the RCLConsensus class, which manages the consensus process in the Ripple (XRPL) ledger system. It defines the RCLConsensus and its nested Adaptor class, which acts as an interface between the consensus engine and the rest of the application. The Adaptor handles acquiring ledgers and transaction sets, sharing proposals and transactions with peers, proposing new ledgers, managing open transactions, and tracking consensus state. It also manages the process of closing and accepting ledgers, including building new ledgers, applying transactions, handling disputes, and validating ledgers. The file includes mechanisms for voting on fees and amendments, handling negative UNL (Unique Node List) votes, and detecting potential censorship of transactions. It provides detailed logging and status notifications to peers, and manages validator keys and operating modes. The RclConsensusLogger class is used for detailed timing and logging of consensus events. Overall, this file is central to the operation of distributed consensus in the XRPL node software, coordinating ledger agreement, transaction application, and network communication during consensus rounds.

This file defines the ConsensusParms struct, which encapsulates various configuration parameters for the consensus process in the Ripple (XRPL) system. These parameters include timeouts and intervals for validation and proposal freshness, minimum consensus percentages, ledger timing constraints, and settings for the Avalanche consensus state machine. The AvalancheState enum and AvalancheCutoff struct are used to manage state transitions during consensus, with a map defining cutoff thresholds for each state. The file also provides the getNeededWeight function, which determines the required consensus percentage and potential next state based on the current state, elapsed time, and round counts. Overall, the file centralizes consensus-related constants and logic to facilitate robust and tunable consensus operations.

This file implements the OrderBookDB class, which manages the in-memory representation of order books in the XRPLedger node. It provides mechanisms to set up and update the order book database from a given ledger, add new order books, query books by taker pays issue and domain, check if a book is to XRP, and manage listeners for order book changes. The update process scans ledger entries for order book directories and AMM pools, populating internal data structures for fast lookup. The class also processes transactions to notify listeners of changes to relevant order books. Thread safety is ensured via locking, and updates are scheduled via the job queue when not in standalone mode. The design supports efficient pathfinding and real-time order book monitoring in the XRPLedger network.

This header file defines the STTx class, which represents a signed transaction in the XRP Ledger protocol. The class inherits from STObject and CountedObject, and encapsulates transaction data, type, and ID. It provides constructors for various initialization methods, including from serialized data and custom assembly functions. The class supports single and multi-signature transactions, with methods for signing, signature verification, and extracting transaction details such as type, sequence, mentioned accounts, and transaction ID. It also includes methods for JSON serialization, SQL metadata generation, and batch transaction handling. The file defines transaction SQL status enums, and provides utility functions for local checks, transaction sterilization, and pseudo-transaction identification. The design enforces canonical signatures and supports protocol rule checks for expanded signer lists.

This file defines the Transaction class and related types for handling transactions in the Ripple (XRPL) server. The Transaction class encapsulates a transaction's data, status, result, and provides methods for managing its lifecycle, including construction from SQL, status management, result setting, and JSON serialization. It tracks transaction state (such as whether it is new, included, conflicted, etc.), supports marking as applying, and manages submission results (applied, broadcast, queued, kept). The class also stores and provides access to current ledger state relevant to the transaction. Static methods allow loading and locating transactions by ID, including searching within ledger ranges. Supporting structures include enums for transaction status, a struct for submission results, a struct for current ledger state, and a locator for transaction search results. The file includes necessary dependencies and forward declarations for integration with the broader application.
